question: Does existing evidence show that a small allowed ID2 rotation produces an image displacement larger than the frozen T_motion of 1.0 px?
extrinsic_basis: PROJECT-STATUS T_base_camera 없음. P-006 BLOCKED. README hand-eye 미측정. P-007F-07A와 P-007F-04가 같은 부재를 이미 기록.
not_an_extrinsic: P-007F-07C solvePnP marker pose in the color camera (marker, not the robot base)
why_projection_was_not_run: Image displacement needs the marker motion in the camera frame. FK supplies motion in the robot base frame. The rigid transform between those frames is not in the evidence. Filling it with a guessed camera pose is forbidden.
why_no_lower_bound: Over an unknown camera orientation, a rotation can move the marker along the viewing ray. The first-order image displacement of that point is then 0. The listed evidence does not exclude that direction, so a positive lower bound is not justified.

id2_joint.frame_of_axis: robot base via FK, not the camera

m2_downstream.link_identity: Arm2_Link end or Arm3_Link start, not resolved

m2_range_m.what_it_locates: marker origin in the color camera

free_quantities_that_can_change_the_verd: camera orientation relative to the robot base
camera position relative to the robot base
metric offset from the ID2 axis to the marker
which downstream link the bracket belongs to
